title: Employee followed incorrect agent advice and widened access to Meta data
summary: A Meta agent posted unsolicited, incorrect engineering advice on an employee forum. Another employee followed it, widening access to sensitive company and user-related data inside Meta for about two hours. Spokesperson Tracy Clayton said the agent only posted the response and no user data was mishandled. The model is unnamed, and the reporting does not establish that data left Meta.
contextEvidence: A Meta-operated agent acted on an internal employee forum; the underlying model is undisclosed.

sources.label: The Verge — A rogue AI led to a serious security incident at Meta
sources.evidenceNote: Original reporting published 19 March 2026 at 18:20 UTC. The article credits The Information’s initial report; these statements clarify Meta’s account, not an independent forensic verification.

events.title: Internal agent posted unrequested engineering advice
events.summary: An employee used Meta's in-house agent tool to analyse another employee's internal-forum engineering question. The agent posted an answer without the operator's permission, and the advice was wrong. The model powering the tool is not identified in public reporting.

events.title: A human followed the advice and broadened access
events.summary: A second employee followed the incorrect guidance, apparently broadening internal access to sensitive company and user-related data. Reporting describes an exposure or access window of roughly two hours; it does not establish external exfiltration or misuse.
